stories.title: Delhi launches mental health policy for students
stories.summary: The Delhi government has launched EHSAAS 2026, a policy aimed at providing emotional support to over 45 lakh students. The initiative includes appointing one counsellor for every 500 students and establishing a 24-hour mental health helpline. The policy seeks to create a supportive environment in educational institutions.

stories.title: Training initiatives show modest impact on workplace practices
stories.summary: Research published in Frontiers in Health Services indicates that multi-sector training can improve practitioner competence in early childhood mental health. While participants reported increased knowledge and confidence, changes in everyday workplace practices remained modest. The study highlights persistent organizational barriers to implementing these skills in professional settings.

stories.title: Mental health first aid in the workplace
stories.summary: Huhtamaki is highlighting the role of everyday conversations in supporting employee wellbeing during Men’s Health Awareness Month. Senior manager Graham Morwood, a trained Mental Health First Aider, notes that the training helps colleagues identify and address challenges. The company views support as tied to safety and care.

stories.title: Jamia Millia Islamia introduces WhatsApp mental health support
stories.summary: Jamia Millia Islamia has launched a WhatsApp-based mental health helpline and a peer support programme for students. The initiative, developed with the Society for the Promotion of Youth and Masses, trains student volunteers to assist peers in distress, with additional support provided by faculty mentors and counsellors.

stories.title: Discovery Colleges adapt recovery models for youth
stories.summary: A narrative review in the International Journal of Mental Health Systems examines the adaptation of adult Recovery Colleges for youth mental health. These educational models aim to provide non-clinical, developmentally appropriate learning environments to address rising demand and workforce shortages in global psychiatric systems.

stories.title: HHS faces internal mental health crisis
stories.summary: The Department of Health and Human Services is experiencing an internal mental health crisis following reports of workplace trauma and suicides. The recent death of an employee at the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration has intensified concerns regarding the department's internal culture and support systems.

Wasatch Back nonprofits receive mental health grants
stories.summary: The Katz Amsterdam Foundation has awarded $500,000 to the Park City Community Foundation as part of a $3.5 million national grant package. The funds will be distributed among eight local nonprofits to support bilingual therapy, behavioral health services, and substance use programs for the community.

stories.title: UAlbany receives federal grant for student mental health
stories.summary: The University at Albany has been awarded a $500,000 grant from the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration. The four-year award will fund Project REACH, an initiative designed to coordinate campus-wide suicide prevention efforts and improve access to mental health resources for the student population.

stories.title: Concordia University hosts sound bath sessions
stories.summary: Concordia University recently invited a practitioner to lead a 30-minute sound bath workshop at the R. Howard Webster Library. The event used auditory vibrations to help students manage stress. The university intends for these sessions to provide a brief, meditative break during busy academic schedules.

stories.title: HIKARU LIFT combines facial sculpting with mindfulness
stories.summary: Entrepreneur Fernanda Casasbuenas has launched HIKARU LIFT, a brand offering stainless-steel facial sculpting tools paired with guided wellness rituals. The company aims to integrate physical beauty with emotional well-being, drawing on the founder's personal experience with facial paralysis to explore the mind-body connection in self-care.

IIT Jodhpur study links meditation to drug effects
stories.summary: Researchers at IIT Jodhpur have identified biological similarities between the effects of meditation and those of 438 different drugs. The study suggests that meditation may produce measurable biological changes in the body, offering new insights into how these processes align with mechanisms targeted by pharmaceutical medicines.

stories.title: IIT Jodhpur research links meditation to drug-like brain activity
stories.summary: Researchers at IIT Jodhpur published a study in Frontiers in Human Neuroscience exploring meditation as a bioactive intervention. The team used connectivity mapping and neurophysiology to investigate how meditation might mirror the effects of brain-active drugs. The study aims to map translational potential through these biological markers.

stories.title: Oxygenation metrics may track sleep apnea severity
stories.summary: A study in Frontiers in Sleep suggests that routine nocturnal oxygenation metrics, such as nadir SpO2 and time spent below ninety percent saturation, may better reflect the physiological burden of sleep apnea than the standard apnea-hypopnea index. Clinical evaluation currently relies on the latter as the conventional standard.

stories.title: Cooling comforter market shifts to year-round demand
stories.summary: The global cooling comforter market is moving from a seasonal niche to a year-round essential, according to an IndexBox report. Demand is increasingly driven by consumer interest in thermal regulation as a wellness need. The category is now bifurcating into mass-market private labels and premium, benefit-driven offerings.

stories.title: Brain patch prototype accelerates REM sleep
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Texas at Austin tested a temple-worn patch that uses ultrasound to influence sleep cycles. In a 28-person experiment, the device helped participants reach REM sleep 43 minutes earlier. The patch aims to alter brain activity without the use of pills or implanted electrodes.

stories.title: Boredom is closely related to poor sleep - Medical Xpress
Financial incentives linked to improved student sleep
stories.summary: Researchers from the University of Pittsburgh, UC San Diego, and other institutions investigated whether small financial rewards could encourage students to improve their sleep habits. The study, published in July 2026, explored the impact of these incentives on the rest patterns of students who struggle to sleep.

stories.title: This Beautiful New England State Was Named the Best Place in America for a Good Night’s Sleep, According to a New Study
Timed Bursts of Pink Noise Boosted Brain Fluid Flow During Sleep in a Small Study - Around Prague
Sound sleep may protect brain health in patients with chronic conditions
stories.summary: A study from the Karolinska Institute suggests that quality sleep may mitigate the cognitive impact of heart disease, stroke, and diabetes. Patients with these conditions who slept well maintained better memory skills and larger brain volumes than those who slept poorly. Sleep is presented as a potential buffer.

stories.title: MIT study finds aging slows brain waste clearance during sleep - NewsBytes
Aging linked to decline in brain waste-removal system
stories.summary: MIT researchers found that the brain's waste-removal process becomes less effective with age, potentially increasing dementia risks. The decline is associated with weaker deep-sleep brain waves and reduced blood flow. Some older adults, however, appear to retain the powerful cleansing waves typically observed in younger individuals.

stories.title: Study links deep sleep waves to brain waste clearance
stories.summary: Research published in Nature Aging suggests that slow electrical waves during deep sleep drive the flow of cerebrospinal fluid to flush waste from the brain. The study compared adults aged 18 to 39 with those aged 60 to 84, finding weaker fluid responses in some older participants.

stories.title: Radiographic markers may predict knee injury risks
stories.summary: A systematic review of 17 studies involving 1,348 patients found that lateral plateau depression and widening can serve as predictors for soft-tissue injuries following tibial plateau fractures. While CT scans and radiographs are standard for bone assessment, their utility for indicating concurrent ligamentous pathology has historically been limited.

stories.title: The Best Colleges for Kinesiology in Idaho 2027
stories.summary: The College of Idaho, the University of Idaho and BYU-Idaho top this 2027 list of the best colleges for kinesiology and physical therapy in Idaho. If you want a career in fitness and health, Idaho has options from the College of Idaho and the University of Idaho to Boise State

stories.title: Healthy lifestyle linked to musculoskeletal health in large study
stories.summary: A cross-sectional study of 21,340 Han Chinese adults identified associations between healthy lifestyle choices, phase angle measurements, and musculoskeletal health. Researchers used bioelectrical impedance analysis to examine how these factors relate to muscle strength and bone status, providing data on the drivers of musculoskeletal aging.

stories.title: School exercise program tests fat but fit concept
stories.summary: Researchers investigated whether an eight-week school-based HIIT program could improve cardiovascular health in adolescents regardless of their baseline weight status. The study, published in Scientific Reports, examined the relationship between physical fitness, body composition, and performance to evaluate the validity of the fat but fit concept.

stories.title: Weight training shows limited muscle preservation on GLP-1 drugs
stories.summary: A study of 120 adults taking Zepbound or Mounjaro found that weight training preserved little muscle mass over nine months. While experts recommend lifting weights to counter muscle loss associated with GLP-1 medications, the findings suggest that the practice may not be as effective as previously assumed.

stories.title: Lifting weights on a GLP-1 is critical , but not because it saves muscle - The Washington Post
Whole-body electromyostimulation shows mild results in pilot study
stories.summary: A pilot study in the Bulletin of Faculty of Physical Therapy found that a single session of whole-body electromyostimulation induces mild, reversible muscle responses in sedentary older men. Researchers suggest the method is safe for those with low activity levels. The muscles were stimulated to move without much effort.

stories.title: Trainers Agree: Walking Won't Keep Your Balance Sharp After 70. These 5 Chair Exercises Will - Eat This Not That
Nutritionist says breakfast variety matters less than quality
stories.summary: Lakshmi Kale, head nutritionist at Nutrition In Sync, suggests that eating the same breakfast daily is not inherently harmful. According to Kale, the primary concern is not the repetition of a meal, but the nutritional quality of the food chosen. Variety is apparently secondary to content.

stories.title: Kimchi probiotics show potential for nanoplastic removal in lab models
stories.summary: A study indicates that specific lactic acid bacteria found in kimchi may help clear nanoplastics from the gut. The research remains in early stages, having been conducted only in laboratory models and mice. Human efficacy has not yet been confirmed. The gut is currently being asked to multitask.

stories.title: Daily iron pills reduce anemia risk but do not boost growth
stories.summary: A Cochrane review of 114 studies involving over 50,000 children found that daily iron supplementation significantly lowers the risk of anemia. However, the supplements did not improve growth or protect against common illnesses. The intervention successfully addressed iron levels, but little else changed for the participants.

stories.title: Perth Children’s Hospital begins study on metabolic cart accuracy
stories.summary: Standard predictive equations for energy expenditure in paediatric intensive care units are accurate only one third of the time. The ICONIC-1 study at Perth Children’s Hospital is now evaluating the clinical utility of modern metabolic carts. The hospital is looking for a more reliable way to count calories.

stories.title: Creatine supplement use nearly doubles among US college students, new study finds - Medical Xpress
Keto diets high in long-chain fats may promote inflammation
stories.summary: A study using mouse and human tissue models suggests the ketogenic diet may be pro-inflammatory. Researchers found that consuming fats featuring long-chain saturated fatty acids can trigger an inflammatory response. The diet that burns fat as fuel may also be heating up the body's internal systems.

stories.title: Study finds lean ground pork triggers muscle-building peptide - National Hog Farmer
FUELED Wellness + Nutrition | Pasta Swaps: lower crab, high protein and more - WGNO
Your Gut Bacteria Make a Compound That Shrank Colon Tumors - Dr. Axe
Nighttime eating habits linked to poor sleep in study of 1,200 women
stories.summary: Researchers surveyed 1,203 women in Türkiye regarding their nighttime eating habits and sleep quality. The study found a connection between waking up to eat and reported sleep issues. Participants were measured for various physical markers to see how hunger might be disrupting their rest cycles at night.

stories.title: Hospitality sector pivots toward wellness and longevity
stories.summary: Hospitality brands are increasingly marketing wellness as a core component of the guest experience. During a recent panel in Milan, executives from Wellness Holding and the Arsenale Group discussed integrating health trends into luxury travel. The industry is now aiming to help guests live better, not just longer.

stories.title: Gut microbe patterns identified in centenarians
stories.summary: A study in Cell Metabolism suggests that changes in gut bacteria as people age may be protective adaptations. Researchers at the University of California San Diego found that microbes modifying bile acids help maintain metabolic function. Longevity may be hidden in how the body digests its own fats.

stories.title: Engineered bacteria improve metabolism in aged mice
stories.summary: Researchers found that amplifying specific gut microbial activity associated with human longevity improved metabolic health in aged mice. Published in Cell Metabolism, the study suggests age-related changes in the gut are protective rather than signs of decline. Scientists are now attempting to engineer a longer lifespan.

stories.title: Review calls for global standards in longevity medicine
stories.summary: A review in Frontiers in Aging identifies a lack of standardized protocols for monitoring healthy adults aged thirty to eighty. Authors propose a global consensus to establish a tiered framework for longevity medicine. The field has grown thirty-five-fold in publications, but remains without a universal assessment tool.

stories.title: dsm-firmenich frames gut health as longevity command center
stories.summary: At SupplySide Global 2026, dsm-firmenich presented the gut as the body's command center for aging. The company cited a trial where supplements and light exercise slowed biological aging by three months. The gut has been promoted to a position of executive authority over the aging process.

stories.title: Enzyme baths gain attention as a wellness trend
stories.summary: Enzyme baths involve submerging in a mixture of rice bran, sawdust, and plant extracts. Proponents suggest the practice helps calm the mind and offers skincare benefits. The treatment is currently gaining visibility through social media, where it is presented as a unique Japanese wellness experience.

stories.title: Meta-analysis reviews acupuncture for autism
stories.summary: A systematic review in Innovations in Acupuncture and Medicine evaluated nineteen randomized controlled trials regarding acupuncture for children with autism. The synthesis reported improvements in core symptoms, including social communication and stereotyped behaviors, when the therapy was combined with conventional rehabilitation methods.

stories.title: Wagweda Ayurveda launches six-product wellness range
stories.summary: Wagweda Ayurveda is introducing a six-product portfolio covering skincare, herbal tea, massage, and oral care. The collection uses a consistent botanical visual identity to market traditional Ayurvedic formats. Each product is positioned to offer consumers a single brand for exploring various self-care categories.

stories.title: Baby Forest expands luxury baby care retail footprint
stories.summary: Baby Forest is opening new stores in Jaipur, Lucknow, and Chandigarh, bringing its total to eight exclusive outlets. The brand targets emerging markets where parents are increasingly prioritizing premium, Ayurveda-inspired products. The expansion aims to provide consumers with opportunities to interact with the brand firsthand.

stories.title: International Men's Day highlights health awareness
stories.summary: International Men's Day on November 19 focuses on health issues including cardiovascular risks, diabetes, and hypertension. The observance encourages regular screenings and lifestyle management. Various Ayurvedic tips and product recommendations are being promoted to address these concerns among the modern male population.

stories.title: Review finds low evidence for Ayurvedic neuropathy treatments
stories.summary: A critical review in Frontiers in Endocrinology examined human clinical literature on Ayurvedic interventions for diabetic peripheral neuropathy. The study found the field dominated by low-quality, uncontrolled reports, concluding there is insufficient evidence to support these treatments as replacements or additions to standard clinical care.

stories.title: Study tracks real-world outcomes of psilocybin therapy
stories.summary: A study of Oregon's state-regulated psilocybin program reports decreased symptoms of mental illness following supervised use of hallucinogenic mushrooms. Researchers describe the findings as a glimpse into real-world outcomes for patients grappling with depression. The therapy remains a subject of ongoing clinical observation.

stories.title: Ayurveda market projected to reach 720 billion dollars
stories.summary: Fact.MR projects the global Ayurveda market will grow from 121.4 billion dollars in 2026 to 720.7 billion dollars by 2036. Classical formulations currently account for 46 percent of the market share. The industry expects to create 599.4 billion dollars in additional value over the next decade.

stories.title: Baby Forest increases physical retail presence
stories.summary: Luxury baby care brand Baby Forest is expanding into Jaipur, Lucknow, and Chandigarh, growing its network to eight exclusive stores. The company is targeting high-potential Indian markets to meet rising demand for premium, Ayurveda-inspired products. The brand intends to build presence through direct consumer interaction.

research.title: Voyager 1, one light-day away from earth today, is a marvel of science
research.summary: Measurements lying in the shadows of their successors can find new lives in the light of new theories. The Voyager 1 mission’s longevity made that more apparent, allowing successive generations of researchers to find more uses for its data even as it continues to collect new information
